key_insight: ROSE-HEA improves high-entropy alloy strength prediction by selecting informative measurements through outcome-aware, robust sequential learning.
engineering_relevance: More sample-efficient ultimate tensile strength prediction could guide alloy composition and processing decisions while reducing costly tensile-testing needs.
method: Predict strength from alloy composition and processing using complementary Gaussian process models.
Anticipate how possible strength outcomes would update predictions and model support.
Select candidates that minimize worst-case expected predictive risk across a reference domain.
evidence_signal: In retrospective tests on 501 HEA records across 30 matched runs, ROSE-HEA reached 152.84 MPa mean RMSE and 0.7443 mean R² with 125 observations, outperforming EI and UCB and surpassing the strongest conventional regressor using 32.4% fewer training observations.
watch_item: Retrospective gains require prospective experimental validation before assuming comparable savings in real alloy-development campaigns.
paper_title: Sample-efficient prediction of high-entropy alloy strength through outcome-aware robust sequential learning
